Get the estimates of other effects in an edge model

Source: R/effects.R
get_effects.Rd

Edge weight models can include effects other than the edge weights: fixed effects, random effects, partial pooling and zero inflation (see bison_model()). This function returns their posterior medians and credible intervals in a data frame. A fixed effect is a single estimated effect of a variable, such as age difference. A random effect estimates a separate value for each level of a grouping variable, such as location, with the values assumed to come from a shared normal distribution.

Usage

get_effects(obj, ci = 0.9)

Arguments

obj

A fitted bison_model object, fitted with Stan (conjugate models only estimate edge weights).

ci

Width of the credible interval, e.g. 0.9 for a 90% interval.

Value

A data frame with columns effect, type, median, and the lower and upper bounds of the credible interval (named after their quantiles, e.g. 5% and 95%). It has no rows if the model has no effects other than edge weights.

Details

The type column says what each row is:

  • "fixed": a fixed effect, such as age for a numeric column, or sex = F for one level of a factor. These are on the same scale as the edge weights before they are transformed: log-odds for binary models and log rates for count models.

  • "random": the random effect for one level of a group, such as location = 2, on the same scale as fixed effects.

  • "random sd": the standard deviation of the random effects in a group.

  • "pooling sd": with partial_pooling = TRUE, the standard deviation of the edge weights.

  • "zero inflation": with zero_inflated = TRUE, the probability that an observation is a structural zero.

See also

get_edgelist() for the edge weights, and summary.bison_model(), which shows both.

Examples

sim_data <- simulate_bison_model("binary", aggregated = FALSE)
df <- sim_data$df_sim
df$location <- factor(df$location)
fit_edge <- bison_model(
  (event | effort) ~ dyad(node_1_id, node_2_id) + age_diff + (1 | location),
  data = df,
  model_type = "binary",
  priors = get_default_priors("binary")
)
#> Running MCMC with 4 parallel chains...
#> 
#> Chain 1 finished in 1.0 seconds.
#> Chain 2 finished in 1.1 seconds.
#> Chain 3 finished in 1.1 seconds.
#> Chain 4 finished in 1.1 seconds.
#> 
#> All 4 chains finished successfully.
#> Mean chain execution time: 1.1 seconds.
#> Total execution time: 1.2 seconds.
#> 
get_effects(fit_edge)
#>         effect      type median     5%    95%
#> 1     age_diff     fixed  0.267  0.087  0.444
#> 2 location = 1    random -0.355 -1.414  0.583
#> 3 location = 2    random  0.043 -0.964  1.043
#> 4 location = 3    random  1.291  0.118  2.722
#> 5 location = 4    random -1.527 -2.649 -0.423
#> 6 location = 5    random -0.052 -1.107  0.997
#> 7 sd(location) random sd  1.099  0.507  1.918
